questions.q: What does a blank accountCode on a company mean in practice?
o: The account is dormant
The account cannot be reconciled against real orders in Intact
The account has no contacts
Nothing — it is optional metadata
questions.e: accountCode is the Intact join key. Without it the company cannot be matched to actual trading history.

questions.q: Someone asks for the value of the pipeline for a board pack. What should you do first?
o: Read the tile and send the number
Check how many open deals carry no amount, and whether the sweep is fresh
Add up the deals by hand
Use the weighted figure instead, since it is smaller
questions.e: Sanity-check before you quote. Deals without an amount are simply absent from the total, and a stale pipeline sweep means the CRM amounts have drifted from the reps' sheets.

questions.q: You think someone else may have seen your credential. What do you do?
o: Watch for anything odd and report it if it happens
Tell Stephen straight away
Change your CRM password
Nothing, it is probably fine
questions.e: Report it immediately so it can be withdrawn and replaced. Nobody minds a false alarm; waiting for evidence is the expensive option.

questions.q: Which view do Customer Operations start the day on?
o: Open Pipeline
All Open (SLA)
Resolved - Last 30 Days
Recently Added
questions.e: All Open (SLA) is the live case worklist, sorted by due date so the most urgent sits at the top. Unowned and Overdue are then driven to zero.

questions.q: What does putting '(Sales Pipe mail)' in the subject of a forward to sales@ do?
o: Nothing, it is just a label
The automation reads it and updates or creates the right deal or case, or raises a review task if unsure
It marks the email as urgent
It sends it to everyone in sales
questions.e: The automation matches the mail against open deals and cases. It can update an opportunity, resolve a case or create a new opportunity - and anything it cannot match confidently becomes a review task rather than a guess.

questions.q: You are logging a deal where a reseller is supplying kit to a large grocery chain. What goes in Company?
o: The grocery chain
The reseller we invoice
Whichever is bigger
Both, separated by a slash
questions.e: Company is the trade account we invoice. The grocery chain goes in End Customer, which is what lets competing resellers chasing the same site roll up in one view.

questions.q: Which of these is the safest way to avoid creating a duplicate company?
o: Search the full legal name from their PO
Search a short distinctive fragment and a couple of variants
Scroll the Companies list alphabetically
Ask a colleague if they remember the customer
questions.e: Short fragments catch variants in spacing, plurals and capitalisation — which is exactly where every duplicate we carry came from.

questions.q: A task is titled 'Sales mtg W28 #7 - Chase Urovo on DT50S lead times'. Where did it come from?
o: A colleague typed it in
The weekly sales meeting action register, ingested automatically
The cadence engine
The Ops Pulse auto-case creation
questions.e: Weekly sales-meeting minutes are turned into Tasks automatically. The W-number is the meeting week and the #number is that action's permanent id, kept for its whole life even when it is carried forward.

questions.scenario: You search Companies for a customer and get two hits: STL Technology Solutions with three open opportunities and a Sales Rep set, and a second STL Technology Solutions with nothing on it. You need to log a new enquiry today.
o: Use the empty record — it is cleaner
Create a third record with a clearer name
Work in the record that holds the open opportunities and flag the duplicate for cleanup
Log the enquiry against both so it is not missed
questions.e: Always work in the record with the history and an owner, so one customer's deals do not get split across twins. Then flag the empty duplicate rather than silently leaving it to catch the next person.
